provenance: Essays and reference annotations written by the OpenPath development team (an AI assistant) for testing. They are NOT educator-validated: no teacher has reviewed them. Agreement with these annotations measures agreement with one synthetic reference, not with educators.

conventions.kind: error = a genuine error a Grade 8 teacher would correct; style = a preference, not an error; strength = done clearly well
conventions.optional: an ambiguous or debatable annotation: matching it counts as agreement, missing it is not penalised
conventions.acceptAlso: other competencies that also count as a match for the same place
conventions.acceptKinds: kinds that count as a match (default: the annotation's kind)
conventions.slip: a single lapse where the form is correct elsewhere
conventions.must_not_flag: valid text (often a valid alternative) that must not be reported as an error

essays.prompt: How do students in your town get to school?
essays.text: Every morning my sister walk to school with her friends. She say the road is safe, but the traffic near the market are heavy. My parents worries about her. The school bus come at seven, but it is always full. I think the town need a new bus route for students. Then everyone could reach school safely and on time.

annotations.quote: the traffic near the market are
annotations.note: The subject is traffic (singular); the verb agrees with market's neighbour.

focus: tense consistency in a past narrative
essays.prompt: Describe a day out with your family.
essays.text: Last Sunday we went to the zoo with our cousins. We saw the elephants first and then we walk to the lion enclosure. The lion was sleeping, so we decide to visit the birds. My little brother laughed when a parrot copies his voice. In the evening we eat ice cream and took a bus home. It was a wonderful day.

annotations.note: The story is in the past: walked.

must_not_flag.why: Past progressive is correct for an ongoing action.

essays.text: I was born on 2012 in a small town near Madurai. My father is an engineer and my mother is teacher. We live at the second floor of an old building. Every summer we go to a beach for a week. I like to swim in the morning and read books on the night. Next year we will move to the Chennai.

annotations.note: A singular job noun needs an article: a teacher.
Floors take on: on the second floor.

must_not_flag.why: "a beach" and "the beach" are both acceptable.

essays.text: Our class planted trees last week it was hard work. Some students dug the holes, others carried water. Because the soil was dry. We used a lot of water. The teacher was pleased, she said the trees would grow quickly. Next month we will plant flowers near the gate.

annotations.quote: Our class planted trees last week it was hard work
Some students dug the holes, others carried water

annotations.note: A subordinate clause on its own is a fragment.

annotations.quote: The teacher was pleased, she said

must_not_flag.quote: Next month we will plant flowers near the gate.

essays.prompt: Describe a mistake you learned from.
essays.text: Yesterday I did a big mistake in my science test. I forgot to make my homework the night before, so I was very nervous. The questions were very hard and I felt very bad. My teacher said I should take more attention in class. Now I will do an effort to study every day.

annotations.note: Vague; a precise word (upset, worried) would be clearer.

essays.prompt: Should mobile phones be allowed in school?
essays.text: Mobile phones should be allowed in school. However, they help students find information quickly. Some students play games in class. Therefore, phones can be useful in an emergency. In conclusion, schools should make clear rules.

annotations.note: However signals contrast, but this sentence supports the claim.
Therefore signals a result that does not follow from the previous sentence.

annotations.quote: Some students play games in class.
annotations.note: A counter-point appears without any signal, so the argument jumps.

must_not_flag.quote: In conclusion, schools should make clear rules.

essays.text: In my opinion, I think that reading books is very important due to the fact that it helps us. At this point in time, many students do not read. Each and every student should read for at least twenty minutes every single day. Reading helps us learn new words and new ideas.

must_not_flag.quote: Reading helps us learn new words and new ideas.

essays.prompt: Write about a place in your school that matters to you.
essays.text: Our school library is small, but it is the busiest room in the building. Students come there before classes, during lunch and after school. The librarian helps us find books that suit our interests. Last month she started a reading club, and twelve students joined in the first week. I hope the school gives the library more space next year.

must_not_flag.quote: before classes, during lunch and after school
must_not_flag.why: A list without a final comma is acceptable.

essays.prompt: What do you think about school uniforms?
essays.text: Different schools have different rules about uniforms, and ours is different from most. We wear a blue shirt and grey trousers. And honestly, nobody minds. The data on student opinions is clear: most of us like the uniform because it saves time in the morning. Everyone has their own style at weekends, so the uniform does not feel boring.

must_not_flag.why: Beginning a sentence with And is acceptable.

must_not_flag.quote: The data on student opinions is clear
must_not_flag.why: Data as a mass noun is acceptable.
British usage, standard in Indian English.

essays.prompt: Describe a city you have visited.
essays.text: When I was ten, I have visited Delhi with my uncle. We have seen the Red Fort and India Gate. The city is crowded, but the people were kind. I would like to go there again, if my parents agree.

annotations.note: A finished time (when I was ten) needs the past simple: I visited.
Part of the same finished trip: we saw.

must_not_flag.why: A present fact about the city is acceptable.

focus: a single slip in correct writing
essays.prompt: Write about someone in your family.
essays.text: My grandfather grows vegetables in a small garden behind our house. He waters the plants every evening and talks to them as if they were friends. My brother and I help him on Sundays. He say that a garden teaches patience. Last year the tomatoes grew so well that we gave some to our neighbours.

annotations.note: He says; the same form is correct elsewhere, so this may be a slip.

essays.prompt: Tell us about a competition you took part in.
essays.text: I am very interested about astronomy. Last month I participated to a science fair at our school. My project depended of a small telescope that my uncle gave me. I explained my results to the judges in the afternoon, and they congratulated me for my work.

annotations.note: Congratulated on is standard; for is also common, so this is debatable.

must_not_flag.quote: explained my results to the judges

essays.prompt: Describe an evening after a match.
essays.text: After the match ended we walked home together. My friend was tired, I was hungry. When we reached my house my mother had made dinner. We ate quickly then we watched a film.

annotations.quote: After the match ended we walked
annotations.note: A comma after an introductory clause helps; many teachers accept it without one.

annotations.quote: My friend was tired, I was hungry
When we reached my house my mother
annotations.note: A comma after the introductory clause is expected here.

annotations.quote: We ate quickly then we watched
annotations.note: Then cannot join two clauses on its own.

essays.text: Although homework can feel tiring, it gives students a chance to practise what they learned in class. Teachers can see which topics need more explanation, and students can work at their own pace. However, too much homework leaves no time for rest or hobbies. Therefore, schools should set short, focused tasks rather than long ones.

annotations.note: A subordinate clause sets up the concession clearly.

essays.text: I had a ice cream and an banana after school. My teacher gave us an useful advice about exams. We need to bring a umbrella tomorrow because it may rain. An hour later, the sky was dark.

annotations.note: Useful starts with a /j/ sound (a useful), and advice is uncountable (useful advice).

must_not_flag.why: An before a silent h is correct.

rewrites.text: Every morning my sister walks to school with her friends. She says the road is safe, but traffic near the market is heavy. My parents worry because the school bus is always full. The town needs a new bus route so that students reach school safely and on time.

My sister likes walking to school with her friends because it is good exercise and she enjoys talking with them. The road near the market is very beautiful in the morning. Everyone in our family enjoys walking together on weekends.
Reading books are very important because it help us learn new word and new idea. Many student do not read now. Every student should reads for twenty minutes each day.
